pr_title: Change files to be deleted in batches instead of one-by-one
pr_body:
Deleting files in object storage one by one is too slow during vacuuming or domain media clean-up. There are batch APIs for S3, and updating rows in a batch instead of one-by-one should be faster, too.

Comparison of clearing out a batch of 100 media attachments:

|Before|After|
|--|--|
|21s|1.2s|

___

Fixes MAS-49

Fix #23073, close #23097
pr_comments: Hi @Gargron - I noticed this failed some lint tests. Shall I fix them in https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/23097?
Ah - I see you've refactored my PR somewhat. I'll leave it in your capable hands.
Hi @Gargron - anything I can do to help move this one along? I can likely fix up the lint errors.

@ClearlyClaire Any reason this wasn't backported to v4.1.x? I guess you have to draw the line somewhere, but this change seems to work just fine on v4.1.11. We currently have it in use and has made the vacuum_scheduler roughly 400 times faster.
We tend to draw the line at actual bugfixes. Furthermore, this PR has proved causing multiple issues that had to be fixed over time.

issue_context.title: Removing large numbers of media files from cloud object storage is very slow
issue_context.body:
### Pitch

Currently, removing large numbers of media files from cloud object storage (S3, and other S3-compatible object stores such as Backblaze B2) is very slow. Mastodon admins [report that deleting 11,000 files takes approximately 1.5 hours](https://ricard.social/@ricard/109551417744385295), compared to [2,000 files in under a minute with local storage](https://troet.eloquer.de/@vash/109552533918829764). Not only does this impact performance, but it needlessly consumes API calls, which are a metered resource on most cloud object storage platforms.

The root cause appears to be that the (kt-)Paperclip library's [`flush_deletes`](https://github.com/kreeti/kt-paperclip/blob/master/lib/paperclip/storage/s3.rb#L411) method deletes objects one by one, rather than taking advantage of the S3 API's [`DeleteObjects`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteObjects.html) action, which allows deletion of up to 1,000 objects per API call:

```ruby
      def flush_deletes #:nodoc:
        @queued_for_delete.uniq.each do |path|
          begin
            log("deleting #{path}")
            s3_bucket.object(path.sub(%r{\A/}, "")).delete
          rescue Aws::Errors::ServiceError => e
            # Ignore this.
          end
        end
        @queued_for_delete = []
      end
```

A fix would be to create batches of 1000 files, and call [`s3_bucket.delete_objects()`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-ruby/v3/api/Aws/S3/Bucket.html#delete_objects-instance_method) for each batch.

I notice that [kt-paperclip](https://github.com/kreeti/kt-paperclip) doesn't seem to be very active, so I'll submit a PR for a monkey patch here as well as a PR for the 'real' fix there.

### Motivation

Any Mastodon admin storing media files in a cloud object store such as S3 or Backblaze B2 will benefit from a fix for this issue.
comments:
Yes, please. Since the process of deleting assets off the object storage is so slow I need to run the cronjob hourly rather than once a day.

Thank you
I think that there’s probably no way to put this functionality into paperclip, but we could add this logic outside of the model where mass-deletes happen. Definitely good idea.

@Gargron It looks like the fix should be in `Paperclip::Storage::S3::flush_deletes`. This is the current code:

```ruby
      def flush_deletes #:nodoc:
        @queued_for_delete.uniq.each do |path|
          begin
            log("deleting #{path}")
            s3_bucket.object(path.sub(%r{\A/}, "")).delete
          rescue Aws::Errors::ServiceError => e
            # Ignore this.
          end
        end
        @queued_for_delete = []
      end
```

This is what I have so far, in [`config/initializers/paperclip.rb`](https://github.com/metadaddy/mastodon/blob/bulk-delete/config/initializers/paperclip.rb#L93):

```ruby
module Paperclip
    module Storage
      module S3Extensions
        OBJECTS_PER_BATCH = 1000 # Defined by https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteObjects.html

        # Batch up deletes. See https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/23073
        def delete_objects(objects)
          begin
            log("deleting #{objects.size} objects")
            s3_bucket.delete_objects({
              delete: {
                objects: objects,
                quiet: true
              }
            })
          rescue Aws::Errors::ServiceError => e
            # Ignore this.
          end
        end

        def flush_deletes
          objects_to_delete = []
          @queued_for_delete.each do |path|
            log("deleting #{path}")
            objects_to_delete.push({key: path.sub(%r{\A/}, "")})
            if objects_to_delete.size == OBJECTS_PER_BATCH
              delete_objects(objects_to_delete)
              objects_to_delete = []
            end
          end
          if objects_to_delete.size > 0
            delete_objects(objects_to_delete)
          end
          @queued_for_delete = []
        end

        # Some S3-compatible providers might not actually be compatible with some APIs
        # used by kt-paperclip, see https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/16822
        if ENV['S3_FORCE_SINGLE_REQUEST'] == 'true'
          #...existing code...
        end
      end
    end
```

I need to build a dev environment so I can test that this indeed fixes the issue.
This won’t do it, this will at most batch 2 or 3 deletes together, because this function is local to a single record.

> This won’t do it, this will at most batch 2 or 3 deletes together, because this function is local to a single record.

Yeah - I realized that last night. `Mastodon::MediaCLI::remove` needs to pause deletes before it loops through the media attachments, and resume them afterwards, ultimately resulting in a call to the `DeleteObjects` action.

I'm thinking that two methods, `startBatch` and `endBatch` should live in `Paperclip::Storage::S3Extensions`, and the `endBatch` method should call `flush_deletes`. Something like this:

```ruby
        def flush_deletes
          unless @deletes_are_paused
            objects_to_delete = []
            @queued_for_delete.each do |path|
              log("deleting #{path}")
              objects_to_delete.push({key: path.sub(%r{\A/}, "")})
              if objects_to_delete.size == OBJECTS_PER_BATCH
                delete_objects(objects_to_delete)
                objects_to_delete = []
              end
            end
            if objects_to_delete.size > 0
              delete_objects(objects_to_delete)
            end
            @queued_for_delete = []
          end
        end

        def start_batch
          log("pausing deletes")
          @deletes_are_paused = true
        end

        def end_batch
          log("resuming deletes")
          @deletes_are_paused = false
          flush_deletes
        end
```

The next question is, how does `Mastodon::MediaCLI::remove()` call `start_batch`? That's what I'm trying to figure out now!
@Gargron I think I've cracked it. See pull request https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/23097.

review_comments: We don't use any Paperclip-managed `created_at` attribute, so this seems unnecessary.

This is not an immediate issue, but in the past we floated the idea of supporting multiple S3 buckets based on object visibility or local VS remote media. This could possibly cause issues in the future. A future-proof alternative may be to group the media attachments per bucket and perform the deletions per bucket.
